sentences.text: Sri G.Srinivasa Rao vs Smt.G.Sreevagdevi on 7 June, 2024

Author: K. Lakshman
Bench: K.Lakshman, P.Sree Sudha
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Lakshman
 And
 The Hon'Ble Smt Justice P.Sree Sudha
 Family Court Appeal No.308 of 2012
 and
 I.A.Nos.1 of 2024 and 2 of 2024
 in/and
 Family Court Appeal No.3 of 2013
Common Judgment

: 
(Per the Hon'ble Sri Justice K.Lakshman) Heard Sri Sivalenka Rama Chandra Prasad, learned counsel for the appellant in F.C.A.No.308 of 2012 and learned counsel for the respondent in F.C.A.No.3 of 2013 and Smt. G.Sreevagdevi, learned party-in-person, respondent in F.C.A.No.308 of 2012 and learned party-in-person, appellant in F.C.A.No.3 of 2013.
2.
The parties hereinafter are referred to as they are arrayed in F.C.A.No.308 of 2012.

3. Smt. G.Sreebagdevi, learned party-in-person had filed a petition vide O.P.No.119 of 2009 against the appellant- husband under Sections 18, 20, 23 and 25 of Hindu 2 KL, J & PSS, J F.C.A.Nos.308 of 2012 and 3 of 2013 Adoptions Maintenance Act, 1960 claiming maintenance for herself and her daughter.
4. According to learned party-in-person, her marriage with the appellant was performed on 25.08.2004 as per Hindu rites and customs.
It is an arranged marriage.
The said marriage was consummated and they were blessed with a daughter by name G.Sridhathri on 06.05.2005.
It is not in dispute that it is second marriage to both of them.
She has narrated several aspects, but the same are not relevant to decide the present appeals.
5. According to learned party-in-person, her husband is working with M/s. Hitachi Home & Life Solutions (India) Ltd. and is drawing an amount of Rs.35,000/- per month towards salary.
Therefore, she is entitled for maintenance of Rs.12,000/- per month and an amount of Rs.1,80,000/- towards arrears.

sentences.text: Appellant-husband filed counter denying the said allegations.
However, he has admitted about the marriage 3 KL, J & PSS, J F.C.A.Nos.308 of 2012 and 3 of 2013 and that they were blessed with a daughter.

The respondent- wife has lodged a complaint with police, who in turn registered a case for the offences under Sections 498A, 494, 495, 403, 406, 420 and 120B of I.P.C and Sections 4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
Even according to him, the marriage of respondent is the second marriage.
Respondent is a practicing advocate.
She is attached to Mr. Rajendran and she is getting remuneration.
Therefore, she is not entitled for maintenance.
7. To prove her claim, respondent examined herself as P.W.1 and filed Exs.P1 to P10.

To disprove the said claim, appellant examined himself as R.W.1 and filed Exs.R1 to R32.
8.

On consideration of entire evidence, both oral and documentary, vide impugned order dated 13.08.2012, learned Family Court allowed the said O.P.No.119 of 2009 in part granting maintenance of Rs.3,000/- per month to the daughter namely Sridhathri from July, 2007 to December, 2008 towards arrears of past maintenance and thereafter she is entitled for present maintenance at Rs.3,000/- per month 4 KL, J & PSS, J F.C.A.Nos.308 of 2012 and 3 of 2013 from January, 2009 till she attains majority and until she is not depend upon anybody.
Learned Family Court also held that the respondent is not entitled for maintenance.
9. Feeling aggrieved by the said order awarding maintenance to daughter, appellant-husband preferred F.C.A.No.308 of 2012.
Respondent-wife preferred an appeal vide F.C.A.No.3 of 2013 seeking enhancement of maintenance i.e., Rs.12,000/- per month to the respondent as well as her daughter.
10. As discussed supra, it is second marriage to both of them.
It is not in dispute that the said marriage between the appellant and respondent was consummated and they were blessed with a daughter by name G.Sridhathri on 06.05.2005.
It is also not in dispute that appellant used to work with M/s.Hitachi Home & Life Solutions (India) Ltd. as Value- Controller (Finance Division).
He has submitted resignation to the said company since the respondent has implicated him in a criminal case and he has faced the said criminal case.
Ex.R27 is the resignation letter.

Therefore,
according to him, 5 KL, J & PSS, J F.C.A.Nos.308 of 2012 and 3 of 2013 he is not doing any job.
Moreover, the respondent is a practicing advocate and she was attached to Mr.Rajendran and she is earning.
He has also taken insurance claim in the name of his daughter.
He made serious efforts to get back his wife and child by issuing legal notice, correspondence etc.
Even in his counter, he has specifically stated that he is interested in leading conjugal life with his wife and he is ready to take his wife and his daughter.
But his wife is not willing.
She is adamant.
Due to the said adamancy, he is deprived of the parental affection.
His life is spoiled.
There is no negligence or willful default on his part.
11. Considering the said aspects, more particularly Exs.R1 to R32 and that he remained unemployed,
learned Family Court came to a conclusion that their daughter's requirement is an amount of Rs.6,000/- per month.

Therefore, appellant and respondent had to share the said expenditure equally and learned Family Court directed the appellant-husband to pay an amount of Rs.3,000/-
per month towards maintenance to his daughter from January, 6 KL, J & PSS, J F.C.A.Nos.308 of Sri G.Srinivasa Rao vs Smt.G.Sreevagdevi on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116861817/
2 2012 and 3 of 2013 2009 till she attains majority and until she is not depend upon anybody.
According to the appellant, his daughter attained majority.
Therefore, she is not entitled for any maintenance.
12. Though the respondent contended that the appellant is working in GVK EMRI as Finance Manager and getting an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- per month, she has not filed any document in proof of the same.
It is the specific case of the appellant that he was resigned from the job and he remained unemployed.
13. It is relevant to note that the appellant is aged about 60 years as of now and respondent is 55 years.
According to the appellant, he has paid the entire arrears as directed by this Court vide interim orders.
In proof of the same, he has filed calculation memo.
His daughter completed B.B.A and L.L.B. She is also earning.
However, she is with the respondent.
7 KL, J & PSS, J F.C.A.Nos.308 of 2012 and 3 of 2013 14.

In the light of the aforesaid discussion and also considering the fact that the daughter of respondent attained majority and she has completed B.B.A and L.L.B, therefore, she is also not entitled for maintenance as per the impugned order.

Therefore, the appeal filed by respondent i.e.,
F.C.A.No.3 of 2013 and the appeal filed by the husband i.e., F.C.A.No.308 of 2012 are liable to be dismissed.

15. During pendency of the appeal, respondent-wife had filed two interlocutory applications i.e.,
I.A.Nos.1 of 2024 and 2 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.3 of 2013 seeking amendment of the grounds of appeal and enhancement of maintenance from Rs.15,000 per month to minor daughter and Rs.10,000/- to respondent-wife.
16. The said appeal is of the year 2013 and she has filed the said Interlocutory Applications in the year 2024, that too, without mentioning satisfactory reasons.
She has not explained the abnormal delay of 11 years in filing the said applications.
As discussed supra, appellant-husband resigned from service and he is not doing any job.
Though 8 KL, J & PSS, J F.C.A.Nos.308 of 2012 and 3 of 2013 the respondent-wife contended that he is working with GVK EMRI at Visakhapatnam, she has not filed any proof.
Therefore, both the applications are liable to be dismissed.
17. Accordingly, F.C.A.No.308 of 2012, F.C.A.No.3 of 2013 and I.A.Nos.1 of 2024 and 2 of 2024 in F.C.A.No.3 of 2013 are dismissed.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending, shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
